solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Relative in medley not half like a schoolgirl

indicators.note: one word sits inside another, placed within its letters
keeping only half of a word means the other half is thrown away

parts.note: a mishmash is a jumbled medley

explanation.surface: Some family member at a gathering is described as acting like a girl at school.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first half of the medley word is used, and the relative sits inside it just before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Missish is an old adjective for prim, affected behaviour supposed typical of a young schoolgirl.

clue.text: Take in booze for going around island

indicators.note: one word travels round another, enclosing it within its letters

parts.note: an alcoholic drink made from honey

explanation.surface: Someone is tricked into drinking on a trip round an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take in' looks like drinking the booze, but it is the definition, in the sense of fooling someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone in is the idiom for deceiving them, which is exactly what misleading does.

clue.text: Cricketers turned up in pink

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning a word up means writing it from bottom to top, backwards

explanation.surface: Cricketers arrive dressed in pink, perhaps for a charity match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pink' looks like a colour but is the verb meaning to pierce, as with a sword point.
explanation.definitionFit: To pink is an old verb for piercing or wounding lightly with a blade, a synonym for stab.

clue.text: Timber is so-so for rebuild

indicators.note: to rebuild is to put the pieces together again in a new form

explanation.surface: Some wood is only average quality for a building project.
explanation.definitionFit: Sissoo is an Indian tree of the rosewood genus prized for its hard, durable wood.

clue.text: One text providing distinctive theories

parts.note: the short message service used for texting

explanation.surface: A single document sets out a particular set of ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: Isms are doctrines or ideologies, informally named from the suffix ending many of them.

clue.text: Melted white stuff present in special stock

indicators.note: one word is placed within the letters of the others

explanation.surface: Something melted and white sits in a special stock, like a cooking instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' and 'melted' suggest a kitchen; the definition is slush from thawed snow.
explanation.definitionFit: Snowbroth is melted snow, slush or snowmelt, so literally liquefied white stuff.

clue.text: Set on schedule in Hollywood

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to timetable or plan something
second meaning: the clapperboard shown before each film take

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a film being on schedule; the second meaning is the film-set clapperboard, also called a slate.
explanation.definitionFit: To slate is to schedule, and in film-making the slate is the board identifying each shot.

clue.text: Lily and Bob Black

parts.note: a bob was a shilling, abbreviated s
Cilla Black, the Liverpool singer and TV presenter

explanation.surface: Seems to list three people: Lily, Bob and someone called Black.
explanation.walkthrough: A bob is slang for the old British shilling, written s; Cilla Black was a British pop singer and TV host.
explanation.definitionFit: Scilla is a genus of bulbous plants of the lily family, including squills.

clue.text: Kidnap a born leader abroad

explanation.surface: A plot to snatch a foreign-born leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Abduce is an obsolete variant of abduct, meaning to lead away by force.

clue.text: Offer to tackle trouble for nightwatchman?

indicators.note: one word grapples with another, wrapping round it

explanation.surface: Someone offers to deal with trouble on behalf of a night security guard.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a nightwatchman is a low-order batsman sent in late in the day to protect better batsmen; the question mark marks the example.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightwatchman in cricket is usually a lower-order batsman, an example of a tailender.

clue.text: High flyer in European capital wanting opening

indicators.note: lacking its opening means the first letter is missing

explanation.surface: A high achiever in a European capital is waiting for an opportunity.
explanation.definitionFit: The erne is the sea eagle, a bird that soars high.

clue.text: Former currency familiar? No mate!

indicators.note: saying no to part of a word means that part is removed

explanation.surface: Someone rejects overfamiliarity over money: 'I'm not your mate!'
explanation.definitionFit: The inti was Peru's monetary unit from 1985 to 1991, replaced by the sol.

clue.text: Navy barracks not right somehow for eatery

indicators.note: arranged somehow means in some unspecified new order
without right means the letter for right is dropped

explanation.surface: The naval base has somehow ended up with a place to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: One R comes out of N + BARRACKS before the remaining letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A snack bar is a small informal eatery serving quick light meals.

clue.text: Cryptic comps said to be irregular

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling or encoded, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Crossword competitions are said to be held only now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Said' tempts a solver to look for a homophone, but it is just part of the letters to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Spasmodic means occurring in fits and starts, at irregular intervals.

clue.text: Broom in butcher's joint altogether lacking width

parts.note: a joint of the leg, as a butcher might sell

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so a letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A broom kept in the butcher's shop, with the joints of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Knee-holly is another name for butcher's broom, a prickly evergreen shrub.

clue.text: Rummy one's seen in village pub

indicators.note: something seen in a place is inside it

explanation.surface: An odd character is spotted in the local village pub.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside PLACE after its P.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin palace is a showy, gaudily decorated pub, originally a Victorian gin shop.

clue.text: Gripe problem disheartened

indicators.note: losing its heart means the central letters are taken out

explanation.surface: A complaint that the problem has got someone down.
explanation.definitionFit: To pule is to whine or whimper, a synonym for grumbling.

clue.text: Two notes about cat put to rest

indicators.note: about means surrounding, enclosing what follows

explanation.surface: Musical notes about a cat that has been buried.
explanation.walkthrough: The two notes are different kinds: one musical, the other the written 'note well' abbreviation, which goes round the cat.
explanation.definitionFit: To entomb is to place a body in a tomb, laying it to rest.

clue.text: Wingless insects seen in middle of hibiscus trees

indicators.note: something seen in another sits inside it
the centre letters of a word are kept

parts.note: the fourth and fifth of eight letters

explanation.surface: Insects without wings found among hibiscus plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilices is the Latin plural of ilex, the holm oak or holly genus of trees.

clue.text: What we are called in explosive games

indicators.note: one phrase is placed inside another word

explanation.surface: A team asks what they are called during a fiery contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A tournament is a sporting competition consisting of a series of games.

clue.text: A number with navy in Mediterranean port act like bullies

indicators.note: these letters are put inside another word

explanation.surface: Sailors and a numbered ship in a Mediterranean port throw their weight about.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyranne is Spenser's verb meaning to tyrannise, to rule or behave as a tyrant.

clue.text: Contracting engineers initially loved to run network test

indicators.note: letters that run are disturbed and spread out of order
initially points to the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: a ping checks a network connection

explanation.surface: Engineers on contract loved running network tests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contracting' reads as engineers on contract, but it is the definition, in the sense of catching an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Developing a cold means contracting it, so the two participles are synonyms here.

clue.text: Quite within variety of Roman garland

indicators.note: within means placed inside

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a particular kind of Roman garland.
explanation.definitionFit: A vallar crown was a Roman award, a garland or crown given to the first soldier over an enemy rampart.

clue.text: Depressing end of tale in Loaded

indicators.note: one letter is placed inside another word
end of picks the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A gloomy ending to a story about being loaded.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaden figuratively means heavy and dull, gloomy or depressing.

clue.text: Dale, one dropping off after a nap and noggin

indicators.note: one falling away means a letter meaning one disappears

explanation.surface: Someone called Dale nods off after a nap and a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping off' and 'nap' suggest sleep; 'noggin' looks like a drink but is the definition, slang for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Noddle and noggin are both informal words for the head.

clue.text: A lodging in Switzerland rented out?

definitions.text: A lodging in Switzerland rented out?

parts.note: property that is let is rented out

explanation.surface: A holiday lodging in the Swiss mountains, available to rent.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition; 'lodging in' is part of the picture and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalet is a Swiss mountain house, often let to holidaymakers.

clue.text: Hearing once behind French lawyer, former Swiss magistrate

indicators.note: behind means coming after, so the first word's letters follow the second's

parts.note: an old legal word for a hearing, as in oyer and terminer

explanation.surface: An old hearing involving a French lawyer and a former Swiss magistrate.
explanation.walkthrough: The hearing is the old legal term from the court of 'oyer and terminer', and the lawyer is the abbreviated French avocat.
explanation.definitionFit: An avoyer was formerly the chief magistrate of certain Swiss cantons such as Bern.

clue.text: Wild onion dish put out fashionably

indicators.note: something put out is ejected, removed from where it was

explanation.surface: A cook throws out a wild-onion dish in a stylish way.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'dish' itself comes out of MODISHLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Moly is a species of wild garlic or onion, Allium moly, with yellow flowers.

clue.text: Clothing racket overturned

indicators.note: in a down entry, overturning a word turns it upside down, so it reads backwards

explanation.surface: A clothing fraud has been exposed and overturned.
explanation.definitionFit: Macs, short for mackintoshes, are raincoats, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Piece of sombre news

indicators.note: part of a phrase, so the letters lie within it

explanation.surface: A bit of gloomy news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece' looks like 'a bit of', but it is slang for a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Piece is slang for a firearm, and the Bren is a British light machine gun.

clue.text: Sanction money restricting Iran primarily

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, enclosing what follows
primarily points to the first letter of the word before

explanation.surface: Financial sanctions are holding back Iran.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiat is an authoritative decree or authorisation, a sanction.

clue.text: Concerned with pre-1918 period, two guys passed over fighting with Germany

indicators.note: passing over something means spanning it on either side

explanation.surface: Two chaps were not picked for the war against Germany before 1918.
explanation.definitionFit: Edwardian refers to the reign of Edward VII, 1901 to 1910, often extended to 1914 or the end of the war.

clue.text: Enclosure in Irish county for carriage

indicators.note: one abbreviation is placed inside a word

parts.note: a county on Ireland's west coast

explanation.surface: A paddock in an Irish county is used for keeping a carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarence is a closed four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage named after the Duke of Clarence.

clue.text: Teach locally in Ulster seaport mostly

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is lost

explanation.surface: Instruction in the local dialect of a Northern Irish port.
explanation.definitionFit: Larn is a dialect form of learn, which regionally also means to teach.

clue.text: Sun cool about not very alluring lady

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, read backwards
without very means the letter for very is dropped

explanation.surface: Sunshine makes a cool woman only mildly attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: Nervy in British use can mean cool or impudent, as well as anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: Syren is an old spelling of siren, a dangerously alluring woman.

clue.text: Fur suit includes rare trim

indicators.note: to include is to take in, enclosing what follows

parts.note: gee is a dialect verb meaning to suit or fit
nett is a rare word meaning trim or neat

explanation.surface: A fur outfit features unusual decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rare' marks NETT as an uncommon sense of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Genette is a variant of genet, the civet-like animal, and its fur.
